## Sample Dataframe

The following code creates a dataframe to test our measures:

```{r}
# Khulna District, mid year 2024 (illustrative figures)
age_group  <- c("15-19", "20-24", "25-29", "30-34",
                 "35-39", "40-44", "45-49")

births     <- c(8000, 15000, 11000, 7000,
                 2200, 600,   100)

female_pop <- c(110000, 105000, 100000, 95000,
                 85000,  75000,  65000)

L5x        <- c(494000, 491000, 488000, 484500,
                 480000, 474000, 466000)  # from a life table, radix 100,000

fert <- data.frame(age_group, births, female_pop, L5x)

# Two more constants we will use later
total_pop <- 2400000     # Khulna mid year total population
p_female  <- 0.487        # proportion of births that are girls (Bangladesh average)
```

## Crude Birth Rate

The formula for Crude Birth Rate is:

$$
CBR = \frac{Total Births}{Total population} \times 1000
$$

To find this for our sample data:
```{r}
births = sum(fert$births)
cbr = births / total_pop * 1000
round(cbr, 2)
```
Here we can understand that per 1000 people 18 children were born in Khulna in 2024.

## Monthly Birth Rate

```{r}
# Khulna, March 2024: 31 days, 3,720 live births recorded
B_month <- 3720
P_month <- 2400000
d       <- 31

MBR <- (365 / d) * B_month / P_month * 1000
round(MBR, 2)
```
Here we can understand that per 1000 people 18 children were born in Khulna in March 2024.

# General Fertility Rate
```{r}
Pf_15_49 <- sum(fert$female_pop)   # 635,000 women aged 15 to 49
GFR <- births / Pf_15_49 * 1000
round(GFR, 2)
```
Which means 1000 women gave births to 69.13 children in 2024 in Khulna.

## A rule of thumb

It is approximately true that: 
$$
GFR = 4 \times CBR
$$

# Age Specific Fertility Rate
```{r}
fert$ASFR <- round(fert$births / fert$female_pop * 1000, 2)
fert[, c("age_group", "ASFR")]
```
We can see the graph:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
plot(fert$ASFR, type = "o", pch = 19, col = "#AA2222",
     xaxt = "n", xlab = "Age group", ylab = "ASFR (per 1000 women)",
     main = "Khulna 2024, Age Specific Fertility")
axis(1, at = 1:7, labels = fert$age_group)
```

# Total Fertility Rate

```{r}
n <- 5                                  # age band width
TFR <- n * sum(fert$ASFR) / 1000
round(TFR, 3)
```
It means a woman in khulna will have 2 children on an average if they lived their full reproductive age.

# Gross Reproduction Rate
The formula is given by:
$$
GRR = TFR \times proportion\ of\ births\ that\ are\ girls
$$

```{r}
GRR <- TFR * p_female
round(GRR, 3)
```
This means each women will give birth to 1.06 daughters if they live upto their full reproductive live

# Net Reproduction Rate

```{r}
l0 <- 100000                                # life table radix

NRR <- sum(fert$ASFR * p_female * fert$L5x / l0) / 1000
round(NRR, 3)
```
